patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with generalized myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine and prednisone, mild asthma and alpha-thalassemia trait. In 2021 a second pregnancy was lost at 26 weeks to parvovirus B19 hydrops; in 2022 persistent parvovirus caused pancytopenia treated with IVIG. Last seen 2026-05-28 for bronchitis, admitted that night in myasthenic crisis.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27F, second-grade teacher, new to the area, here to set up primary care. Old records reviewed (scanned 9/12).

Myasthenia gravis: generalized, diagnosed 2017 by her neurologist, who she will keep seeing (next visit in Nov). Describes herself as "mostly normal" on current regimen. End of the school day she sometimes notices her eyelids feel heavy; resolves with rest and her afternoon pyridostigmine. No swallowing or breathing trouble. Never hospitalized for it.
Asthma: since childhood. Uses albuterol a handful of times a year, mostly with colds or cold air at recess duty. No night symptoms, no ED visits, no oral steroid bursts beyond her daily prednisone.
Alpha thalassemia trait: knows about it; her dad carries it too. Told years ago her blood count always runs a little low.

OB: one child, born early this year, uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery. Pap at her postpartum visit in April was normal.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg every 4-6 h while awake, prednisone 10 mg every morning, albuterol HFA prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with alpha thal trait; mother with autoimmune thyroid disease.
SH: married, one baby at home. Never smoker, no alcohol. Teaches elementary school.

Exam: well-appearing, conversant, no ptosis at rest; sustained upgaze 60 s without fatigue. EOMI, no diplopia. Speech normal. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft. Strength 5/5 proximal and distal. No rash.

A/P
1. Myasthenia gravis, generalized, stable - continue pyridostigmine and prednisone as prescribed by neurology; will refill locally if easier for her. Reviewed warning signs: trouble swallowing, breathing, or speaking -> ED.
2. Asthma, mild intermittent - albuterol prn. 
3. Alpha thalassemia trait - CBC today for her baseline.
4. Long-term prednisone - A1c and CMP today.
5. Health maintenance: CMP, lipids, TSH (mother's thyroid history), one-time HIV and hep C screen. Tdap given. Flu shot when supply arrives. Pap up to date (04/2019).
PHQ-2 0.
Follow up yearly physical, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Malee, your labs from Tuesday are back. Kidney and liver tests, sugar (A1c), cholesterol and thyroid are all normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens negative. Your blood count shows the small red cells and slightly low hemoglobin we expect with alpha thalassemia trait - this is your baseline, and I'll use it to compare going forward. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Neuromuscular Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Visit date: 11/21/2019

Dear colleague, thank you for taking over her primary care.

Ms. Bautista returns for routine review of generalized myasthenia gravis. Since her last visit she reports mild late-afternoon lid heaviness on long days, no diplopia, no bulbar or respiratory symptoms.

Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg every 4-6 hours while awake; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol inhaler as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Examination: no ptosis at rest or after sustained upgaze; extraocular movements full; facial and bulbar strength normal; neck flexion 5/5; limbs 5/5 without fatigable weakness.

Impression: generalized myasthenia gravis, well controlled.
Plan: no change in doses. Reviewed medications that can worsen myasthenia; list given to patient. Return in 6-12 months.

Neuromuscular clinic

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax requesting pyridostigmine 60 mg #180 with refills. Original prescriber is her neurologist; pt asked us to take over refills. Routed to PCP - approved, 90-day supply x 3 refills sent. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Question about getting sick at school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, with everything going around my classroom right now I'm a little nervous since I take prednisone every day. Is there anything I should be doing differently? Thanks, Malee

documents.title: RE: Question about getting sick at school
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Ten milligrams a day does lower your defenses somewhat, so: hand washing, keep up with vaccines, and let us know early if you get sick rather than waiting it out - especially a fever, a cough that is getting worse, or any change in your swallowing, speech or breathing, since infections can stir up myasthenia. Don't stop or skip the prednisone on your own. We're here same day if you need us.

A/P

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here after a positive home pregnancy test. LMP 2/15/21 -> about 3.5 weeks; EDD around 11/22/21. G2P1 (healthy 2-year-old, uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery). Mild nausea, no bleeding or cramping.
MG: stable, same doses, neurologist aware of plans to conceive. Asthma: quiet.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.
Urine hCG positive in office.
Exam: well. No ptosis. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
1. Intrauterine pregnancy, early first trimester - referral to obstetrics placed; she would like an OB close to home. Asked them to see her early given MG and chronic steroid.
2. Myasthenia gravis - continue pyridostigmine and prednisone unchanged; both have been used through her first pregnancy without trouble. Messaging neurology so they know. She has the list of drugs to avoid with MG to share with OB.
3. Asthma - albuterol prn is fine in pregnancy.
She will get her COVID vaccine when teachers become eligible; reviewed that it's recommended in pregnancy.

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of visit: 05/20/2021
GA 13w3d by LMP (2/15/21). G2P1001.

Thank you for referring Ms. Bautista. Pregnancy unremarkable so far. Today she raises two concerns: her belly feels bigger than it did at this point last time, and for about a week she has been a little short of breath.

PMH: generalized myasthenia gravis (neurology), asthma, alpha thalassemia trait.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol HFA prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father alpha thal carrier; mother autoimmune thyroid disease. One healthy child, 2.
Social: elementary school teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

BP 120/75, HR 88, RR 18.
Uterus measures larger than expected for 13 weeks. Fetal heart tones present. Lungs clear.

Labs: Hgb 11 g/dL, Hct 33%, MCV 70 fL. Hemoglobin electrophoresis: HbA 97%, HbA2 2.5%, HbF 0.5% - no beta-chain variant; with the microcytosis, consistent with her known alpha thalassemia trait.
Ultrasound: single live IUP, size equals dates, normal fluid (report attached).

Assessment: IUP at 13 weeks. Size greater than dates on exam, not borne out on ultrasound. Mild dyspnea of pregnancy vs asthma; lungs clear. Alpha thalassemia trait confirmed.
Plan: routine prenatal labs; recheck growth and fluid at next visit in 4 weeks. Will coordinate with neurology.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

reports.conclusion: Fetal hydrops: ascites, skin edema and pericardial effusion, with polyhydramnios and placental thickening.

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of visit: 06/16/2021, with serology addendum 06/18/2021
GA 17w2d.

Follow-up after last month's size-dates question and shortness of breath. She has felt fine overall. Mentions a mild cold around two weeks ago - low-grade temperature, tiredness, stuffy nose - gone on its own within days. No travel. No known sick contacts, though several children in her class have been passing around viral illnesses.

Meds unchanged (pyridostigmine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol prn). NKDA.

Ultrasound today: fetal ascites, skin edema and a small pericardial effusion; polyhydramnios; thick placenta. FHR 165. Follow-up study shows raised MCA peak systolic velocity (reports attached).

Assessment: fetal hydrops with Doppler evidence of fetal anemia at 17 weeks. Infectious cause suspected given classroom exposure and recent illness.
Plan: parvovirus B19 serology sent today. Counseling done; she understands the findings are serious.

ADDENDUM 06/18/2021: parvovirus B19 IgM POSITIVE, IgG NEGATIVE - acute maternal parvovirus B19 infection. Patient informed by phone. Close ultrasound surveillance.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Telephone Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt after reviewing OB letter (fetal hydrops, parvovirus B19 IgM positive). She is frightened but understands what OB told her. Answered questions about the virus - common in schools, not something she did wrong. She asked whether her prednisone made it worse; explained steroids can blunt the immune response, but stopping it now would risk a myasthenia flare - keep taking it, OB and neurology agree. No weakness, swallowing or breathing symptoms. She has OB follow-up set. Told her to call any time; offered to see her. 15 min.

reports.text: Single intrauterine pregnancy, cardiac activity present. Nuchal skin thickening. Pericardial effusion. Fetal ascites.
reports.conclusion: Persistent fetal hydrops: nuchal skin thickening, pericardial effusion and ascites.

OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY - VISIT NOTE
Date of visit: 07/20/2021
GA 22w2d.

Known maternal parvovirus B19 infection about a month ago with fetal hydrops. Comes in early: for the last few days low-grade temperatures, fatigue, and a pink rash on both cheeks. Says several of her students looked the same last week. Because of her job and these symptoms a CBC and ultrasound were done today.

Meds: pyridostigmine, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.
Exam: faint erythematous rash over both cheeks; otherwise unremarkable.
CBC: unremarkable for her.
Ultrasound: nuchal skin thickening, pericardial effusion, ascites (report attached).

Assessment: facial rash consistent with parvovirus; ongoing fetal hydrops at 22 weeks.
Plan: close surveillance; reviewed fetal kick counts and when to go to the hospital.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 07/20/2021 19:05

CC: baby moving less for two days.
HPI: 28-year-old G2P1 at 22 weeks, generalized myasthenia gravis on daily prednisone, seen in her OB's office this morning for a parvovirus rash. Over two days fewer fetal movements. Denies vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage or contractions.
PMH: myasthenia gravis, asthma, alpha thalassemia trait; parvovirus B19 infection this pregnancy with fetal hydrops. Prior pregnancy term, uncomplicated.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.
SH: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Vitals: BP 120/78, HR 88, T 36.8 C.
Exam: comfortable; abdomen gravid, nontender; no vaginal bleeding.

Labs: O positive; antibody screen negative. Hgb 13.2, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000. Parvovirus B19 IgM positive, IgG negative.
OB ultrasound: single fetus, skin edema and ascites; no abruption or previa.
Fetal monitoring: baseline 160 bpm, minimal variability, no accelerations.

MDM: persistent parvovirus B19 viremia without seroconversion five weeks after illness in a patient on chronic corticosteroids - severe infection in an immunocompromised host, with fetal hydrops. Reviewed with on-call obstetrics.
Disposition: discharged 01:30 with close obstetric follow-up and return precautions for absent movement, bleeding or pain.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL LABOR & DELIVERY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 08/16/2021  Discharged 08/18/2021

Reason for admission: no fetal movement for 24 hours at 26w0d.
History: G2P1, generalized myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine and prednisone 10 mg, asthma, alpha thalassemia trait. This pregnancy complicated by maternal parvovirus B19 infection without seroconversion and fetal hydrops. Denied bleeding, abdominal pain, fever or trauma.

On arrival vital signs stable. Abdomen appropriate for gestational age; no fetal heart tones by handheld Doppler. Ultrasound confirmed intrauterine fetal demise with no cardiac activity.
Labs: Hgb 12.2, platelets 250K, PT 12 s, PTT 30 s, fibrinogen 400 mg/dL.

Course: the patient was understandably distraught and asked for time with her family before deciding about management. On 8/17 she chose induction; misoprostol induction, uncomplicated vaginal delivery of a stillborn infant with marked hydrops. Placenta delivered intact. Estimated blood loss small. Blood type O positive - anti-D not indicated. Home medications continued throughout; no myasthenic symptoms. Bereavement and social work support provided.

Discharge diagnoses: intrauterine fetal demise at 26 weeks; fetal hydrops due to maternal parvovirus B19 infection.
Discharge medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn.
Follow-up: obstetrics in 6 weeks; primary care.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Telephone Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called after reading the discharge summary. Expressed our condolences. Physically recovering, bleeding light, no fever. Sleeping poorly. Supportive family around. School starts in two weeks - unsure she's ready but wants the routine. Taking all her medicines. Visit set for mid-September to check in; sooner if needed.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Four weeks after stillbirth at 26 weeks (parvovirus B19 with fetal hydrops). She went back to her classroom last week; says being with the kids helps and also is hard. Sad most days, some crying, sleep improving. Eating ok. No thoughts of self-harm. Leaning on family; considering the hospital's bereavement group.
Bleeding stopped. No fever. No weakness, ptosis, swallowing or breathing trouble. Rash long gone.
Meds: pyridostigmine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol prn.
PHQ-9 6, GAD-7 4.
Exam: tearful at times, appropriate. No ptosis. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
1. Grief after stillbirth - normal grief response, mild symptom scores. No diagnosis. Gave bereavement group and counselor contacts; she'll reach out. Recheck in a couple of months or sooner.
2. MG - stable through delivery.
3. Postpartum check with OB in 2 weeks.
Flu vaccine today.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY - POSTPARTUM VISIT
Date of visit: 09/28/2021

Six weeks after misoprostol induction and vaginal delivery of a stillborn at 26 weeks (fetal hydrops, maternal parvovirus B19). Lochia resolved. No fever or pelvic pain. Coping with grief, has support; seeing her PCP.
Exam: abdomen soft; uterus normal size, nontender; perineum healed.
Assessment: normal postpartum recovery.
Plan: discussed that parvovirus does not usually recur in a later pregnancy; preconception visit when she is ready. Routine gynecologic care through PCP.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

Fluids, rest, acetaminophen as needed, continue all meds including prednisone - do not skip. Call same day if fever climbs, breathing worsens, or any myasthenia symptoms. documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29F with generalized MG on prednisone 10 mg, asthma, alpha thal trait; stillbirth Aug 2021 from parvovirus B19 hydrops.
About a month of being wiped out - napping after school, which isn't her. Bruises on her legs she can't explain, and nosebleeds several times a week, each stopping with pressure in 10 minutes. Had a cold early this month that cleared within the week. No fevers since. No melena, no heavy menses. No weight loss. No new meds or supplements. No ptosis, diplopia, dysphagia or dyspnea.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.

Exam: pale. Conjunctivae pale. No scleral icterus. Nasal mucosa with dried blood on the left, no active bleeding. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Scattered petechiae over both lower legs, a few ecchymoses on the shins. No ptosis, strength full.

A/P
Fatigue, bruising, epistaxis with pallor and petechiae - concern for a marrow problem. CBC with diff and CMP drawn now, asked lab to call results.
Addendum 11:45: lab called - all three cell lines low (see results). Pancytopenia. Discussed with on-call hematology, who will see her tomorrow morning. Spoke with pt: no NSAIDs, nosebleed first aid, ED for heavy bleeding, fever, or any new weakness. She'll stay home from school.
Urgent hematology referral placed.

documents.title: Critical Result Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Lab called critical platelet count on today's CBC; read back and verified. Given to PCP at 11:42. PCP spoke with patient and hematology; appointment tomorrow 9:00 confirmed with pt.

reports.text: Specimen: bone marrow core biopsy and aspirate, posterior iliac crest. The core shows profound hypocellularity with fatty infiltration. Residual hematopoietic elements are sparse. No infiltrating tumor. No granulomas. Aspirate smears paucicellular.
reports.conclusion: Profoundly hypocellular marrow with fatty infiltration.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - NEW CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 02/22/2022

Thank you for the urgent referral of Ms. Bautista, 29, with generalized myasthenia gravis on prednisone 10 mg daily, asthma and alpha thalassemia trait. Six months ago her pregnancy ended in intrauterine fetal demise from parvovirus B19 hydrops. For a month: fatigue, easy bruising, frequent nosebleeds. She had an upper respiratory infection that cleared about two weeks ago.

Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.
Family history: father alpha thal trait; mother autoimmune thyroid disease.
Social: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: pale. Scattered petechiae on the lower extremities. No lymphadenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly.

Labs: Hgb 7.8 g/dL, WBC 2.1 x10^9/L, platelets 20 x10^9/L, reticulocytes 0.5%. Smear: no abnormal cells, no schistocytes.
Bone marrow biopsy (done today): profound hypocellularity with fatty infiltration (pathology attached, finalized 2/25).

Impression: pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow. In a woman on chronic steroids who never formed IgG to parvovirus B19 last summer, persistent B19 infection is the leading cause.
Plan: parvovirus B19 PCR on blood; follow-up next week. Bleeding precautions, no NSAIDs. Threshold for platelet transfusion discussed.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 03/02/2022

Parvovirus B19 DNA PCR from 2/22: DETECTED, 5.2 x 10^10 IU/mL.

Impression: persistent parvovirus B19 infection in a host on chronic prednisone, causing marrow failure with pancytopenia.
Plan: intravenous immune globulin 0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days at our infusion center, 3/7 through 3/11. Prednisone unchanged - discussed with her neurologist; IVIG is also well tolerated in myasthenia. No transfusion needed at present; she has had no further significant bleeding. CBC weekly during and after infusion, visit in about 6 weeks with repeat PCR later.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.body: Just wanted to let you know I finished all five IVIG infusions last week. No problems with them. Hematology says the counts are starting to move. I'm back at school half days. Thank you for getting me in so fast.

documents.title: RE: Finished the infusions
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: So glad to hear it. Keep the half days as long as you need. Let's plan a visit in April after your next hematology appointment.

Heme CBC 4/12: Hgb 10.1, WBC 3.4, plt 112 - reviewed together.
Exam: color better. No petechiae. Lungs clear. No ptosis.
A/P: Pancytopenia improving after IVIG - hematology following with monthly counts; no labs needed here today. MG/asthma stable, meds unchanged. Physical in the fall; Pap due then.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Just turned 30. Teaching full time again, new class of second graders. Feels like herself.
Interval: hematology discharged her last week - B19 PCR undetectable, counts at baseline (CBC 9/20, so not repeated today). MG: stable, no flares through all of it. Asthma: albuterol maybe twice since spring.
Grief: still hard around the anniversary in August; she did go to the bereavement group for a while. Mood ok. Not planning pregnancy right now.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.
PHQ-2 1.

Exam: well. No ptosis, EOM full. Thyroid normal. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions; Pap/HPV collected. Skin without petechiae. No edema.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap with HPV (age 30). CMP, A1c, lipids, TSH. Flu today. On long-term prednisone, so PCV20 today; recommended the 2-dose recombinant shingles series - she'll get dose 1 at the pharmacy with her COVID booster.
- MG, asthma: stable, no changes.
- Parvovirus/pancytopenia: resolved per hematology; CBC with yearly physicals.

documents.title: Lab results

documents.body: Malee - kidney and liver function, sugar, cholesterol and thyroid all normal. The Pap result will follow next week; I'll send it when it's in.

documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Visit date: 03/09/2023

Generalized myasthenia gravis. Eventful two years outside of neurology - pregnancy loss in 2021 from parvovirus B19 and marrow suppression in 2022 treated with IVIG by hematology - yet her myasthenia remained quiet throughout. Today: occasional evening lid heaviness only. No diplopia, bulbar or respiratory symptoms.
Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg every 4-6 hours while awake; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol prn. NKDA.
Exam: no ptosis after sustained upgaze; EOM full; bulbar and facial strength normal; neck flexion 5/5; limbs full without fatigability.
Impression: stable.
Plan: continue current doses. Annual review. She has our after-hours number for any bulbar or breathing change.

Neuromuscular clinic

documents.title: Same-Day Sick Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33F with generalized myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine/prednisone, mild intermittent asthma, alpha thal trait; history of parvovirus B19 (2021 stillbirth, 2022 pancytopenia, resolved).
S: About a week ago low-grade fever and malaise, which went away. Since then five days of cough and mildly short of breath. No chest pain. No vomiting or diarrhea. Has used albuterol a few times this week.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.

O: T 37.2 C (99 F), BP 120/78, P 88, RR 20, SpO2 97% RA.
Scattered wheezes both lungs; no rales, no rhonchi. Rest of exam unremarkable.
CXR PA/lat (in office): no pneumonia, no other abnormality.

A/P
Acute bronchitis after a viral illness, with wheeze in a patient with asthma. No pneumonia on film. Albuterol 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for the next several days; continue prednisone and pyridostigmine. Fluids, rest; okay to finish the school week if she feels up to it. Call or message if not improving in a week, sooner for fever, worsening breathing. Follow-up as needed.

documents.title: ICU Admission Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - MEDICAL ICU ADMISSION NOTE
Date: 05/28/2026 20:30

CC: two days of worsening trouble breathing and swallowing after a respiratory infection.
HPI: 33-year-old with generalized myasthenia gravis, seen by her primary care physician earlier today for cough. Over the past two days her breathing and swallowing have steadily worsened. She had a respiratory infection last week and did not seek care for it until today. Brought in this evening.
Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg q4-6h; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol prn. NKDA.
PMH: myasthenia gravis, asthma, alpha thalassemia trait; parvovirus B19 2021-2022, resolved.
SH: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: bilateral ptosis; reports diplopia. Nasal speech, drooling. Neck flexion 3/5. Shallow breathing, RR 28.
ABG: pH 7.32, PaCO2 50, PaO2 60, HCO3 24.

Impression: myasthenic crisis precipitated by respiratory infection, with hypercapnic respiratory failure.
Plan: intubation for airway protection and ventilation; hold pyridostigmine while intubated; IVIG 2 g/kg divided over 5 days; continue prednisone 10 mg via tube; avoid drugs that worsen myasthenia; neurology consulted.

Pulmonary & Critical Care

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/28/2026 (via ED to medical ICU)  Discharged 06/05/2026

Principal diagnosis: myasthenic crisis.
Secondary: acute bronchitis (precipitant); asthma; alpha thalassemia trait.

Course: Arrived the evening of 5/28 with bulbar weakness, ptosis, neck flexor weakness and hypercapnia (ABG 7.32/50/60/24). Intubated on arrival. Pyridostigmine held. IVIG 2 g/kg given over five days with neurology. Strength improved steadily; extubated 6/2 without difficulty. Pyridostigmine restarted at home dose; swallow normal before diet advanced. Transferred out of ICU 6/3. Walking independently, speech and swallowing at baseline at discharge.

Discharge medications (unchanged from home): pyridostigmine 60 mg every 4-6 hours while awake; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol 2 puffs prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: outpatient neuromuscular clinic in about 6 weeks; primary care in 1-2 weeks. Return for any swallowing, voice or breathing difficulty.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt - heard from her by message that she was home 6/5 after ICU stay for myasthenic crisis; records requested from the hospital. She is home resting, school year is done for her. Voice normal, eating regular food, no choking, breathing comfortable, cough nearly gone. Taking pyridostigmine and prednisone 10 mg as before, has albuterol. Neuromuscular follow-up 7/14. Offered PCP visit next week - booked 6/16. Knows to call 911 for any breathing or swallowing trouble.

OUTSIDE NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Visit date: 07/14/2026

Seen six weeks after ICU admission for myasthenic crisis triggered by a respiratory infection (intubated, IVIG, extubated 6/2, home 6/5). Since discharge she has steadily regained strength. Now back to her baseline: no ptosis, diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia or shortness of breath.
Medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg every 4-6 hours while awake; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol prn. NKDA.
Exam: no ptosis after sustained upgaze; EOM full; speech normal; neck flexion 5/5; limbs 5/5 without fatigability.
Impression: generalized myasthenia gravis, recovered to baseline after crisis.
Plan: same doses. Early care for future respiratory infections. Return in 3 months.

Neuromuscular clinic
